scans.summary: Three themes. The global diesel shortage is far bigger than the Russian diesel deal that knocked energy lower. Chile's copper problems are spreading, and producers outside Chile get the price without the outages. Memory stocks sold off together on China's CXMT, but a strike at Micron's Taiwan fabs would help Samsung and SK Hynix, not hurt them.

Two themes. UnitedHealth says commercial medical cost trend is running above 11% and will persist into 2027; that is revenue for hospitals and a cost for employers that carry their workers' health risk through UnitedHealthcare, such as Insperity. Givaudan's fine fragrance sales grew about 31% in Q3, a supplier signal that perfume brands have not yet traded on.

No new ideas met the bar today. A hotter-than-expected September CPI (3.7%) pushed the 10-year above 5.25% and set off a global tech sell-off (SOX -4.5%, KOSPI about -8%, Nikkei about -5%), while CoreWeave bond yields above 15% and record Oracle CDS spread fears about debt-funded AI build-outs; the read-throughs examined (Mondi to Smurfit Westrock, CMC to Nucor, TSMC to GlobalFoundries, Ericsson and Softcat to memory suppliers) were either already priced, too small, or traded the same day in London. Morgan Stanley's equities growth of 41% trailed Goldman's 72%, closing out the kill condition on that idea.

Two new ideas, both shorts on policy news that broke after Thursday's close and has not been priced. A Fifth Circuit ruling against the body that runs the $9 billion Universal Service Fund threatens GCI, which gets about 40% of its revenue from the fund, and the stalled US-Mexico tariff talks delay demand from Ternium's auto and industrial customers. Read-throughs examined and rejected: auto dealers after the Penske buyout (peers already up 5-9%), FMC's price cuts to American Vanguard and Corteva (micro-cap, or already down), Zijin's Bisha zinc halt (about 0.05% of world supply), and the TSMC and ASML beats (a first-order link that adds to the AI-capex factor).

Two new ideas. The US shadow-fleet proposal would free only about 24 sanctioned supertankers by Kpler's count, yet DHT gave back its whole gain from Q4 bookings at about three times Q3 spot rates; and China's September coal output fell 6.8% while Australian coal exporters rose 4-5% before US-listed Peabody had traded. Read-throughs examined and rejected: West Fraser's softwood duty cut (final rate close to the April preliminary), Aixtron's laser-tool orders to Veeco (Axcelis merger status unclear) and AXT, Disc Medicine's EPP trial win to Clinuvel (no liquid US listing), the Russia sanctions waiver to India (Indian stocks fell on the day), and TSMC's HBM base-die win (first-order, adds to the AI-capex factor). Centinela's strike settlement meets a second part of the SCCO kill condition.

ideas.event: US eases Russian diesel sanctions for six months; Russia to release 4.8 million tons of diesel

source.title: Fortune: Trump strikes a diesel deal with Putin

source2.title: Dallas Fed: Refinery outages pumping up fuel prices

chain: 4.8 million tons of diesel is about 36 million barrels, roughly 200,000 barrels a day over six months.
The Dallas Fed puts lost global refining capacity at 6 to 8 million barrels a day, so the deal covers about 3% of the gap.
Europe's diesel shortage persists and keeps pulling US distillate exports at record margins.
Valero, the largest US refiner with a big Gulf Coast export footprint, keeps earning those margins.
ideas.name: Valero Energy
ideas.priced_in: Crude fell about 2% on the deal and Brent sits near $104. The headline reads as relief; the arithmetic says the shortage barely changes.
ideas.kill: Strait of Hormuz flows normalize, or European diesel margins fall back toward 2022 levels.

ideas.event: Global refining capacity down as much as 10%; Europe importing more US diesel; Russian diesel flows reopening

source.title: Dallas Fed: Refinery outages pumping up fuel prices

chain: Refining has moved away from Europe, and Middle East and Russian plants are damaged.
Diesel now travels farther: US Gulf to Europe, plus reopened Russian flows that must route around sanctioned buyers.
Longer voyages tie up more product tankers, so day rates rise.
Scorpio Tankers runs one of the largest fleets of product tankers.
ideas.name: Scorpio Tankers
ideas.priced_in: Tanker equities price off spot day rates, which lag the route changes. Third-order link, lightly covered.
ideas.kill: Red Sea and Hormuz both reopen, collapsing voyage lengths.

ideas.event: Middle-distillate shortage: diesel above gasoline by a record margin; jet fuel comes from the same barrel

source.title: Dallas Fed: Refinery outages pumping up fuel prices

chain: Jet fuel is a middle distillate, refined from the same part of the barrel as diesel.
If the diesel deal doesn't close the gap, jet fuel stays expensive relative to crude.
Airlines hedge crude more than refined jet fuel, so the crack spread hits margins directly.
This is the other side of the Valero idea: same thesis, opposite exposure.
ideas.name: US airlines ETF
ideas.priced_in: Airlines bounced as crude fell on the diesel headline. The bounce assumes relief that the volumes don't support.
ideas.kill: Jet fuel cracks narrow, or airlines guide fuel costs lower on Q3 calls.
ideas.book: A short. Only execute if your account and compliance allow it; otherwise track it as a signal.

ideas.event: El Teniente pit shut after a deadly landslide; Centinela strike; fatal accident at Escondida; storms at Los Pelambres

source.title: MINING.COM: Chile copper supply under pressure as disruptions mount

chain: An index puts 5.2% of output at Chile's largest copper mines at risk, with El Teniente, Los Pelambres and Escondida highest.
Chilean disruptions support the copper price while cutting Chilean producers' volumes.
Producers outside Chile get the higher price without the lost tonnes.
Southern Copper mines in Peru and Mexico and has the most copper exposure of the large producers.
ideas.name: Southern Copper
ideas.priced_in: Copper is already strong, and Panmure Liberum argues the rally is more financial than physical. That's the main risk. Update Oct 16: Part of the kill condition has been met. Escondida supervisors ratified their contract on Oct 14, and copper fell three straight sessions to about $14,360/t on the LME (its weakest since Oct 5). Centinela workers remain on strike and copper is still above its early-October level, so the full condition has not been met. Update Oct 19: Centinela workers ratified a new contract on Oct 18 with 94.5% approval, so two of the three parts of the kill condition have now been met. LME copper recovered to about $14,500/t on Oct 16 and is still above its early-October level, so the full condition has not been met.
ideas.kill: Centinela settles, Escondida supervisors sign, and copper gives back its October gains.
ideas.book: Replaces some of the copper exposure you had in FCX, without Grasberg risk.

ideas.event: Micron's Taoyuan union voted 99% to authorize a strike; memory stocks sold off on China's CXMT DRAM roadmap

source.title: Digitimes: Micron's Taiwan union wins strike vote

chain: On Oct 13, Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix all fell together on CXMT's DRAM roadmap, a year-end target years from volume.
Separately, a strike at Micron's Taiwan fabs, a large share of its DRAM output, would cut supply from the number three producer.
Less Micron supply means tighter DRAM pricing, which helps the other two producers.
Samsung and SK Hynix are the largest holdings in the Korea ETF.
ideas.name: South Korea ETF
ideas.priced_in: The market sold the whole group as one trade. A strike would split them.
ideas.kill: Micron and the union settle, or DRAM contract prices roll over.
ideas.book: Memory is AI-adjacent; counts toward the AI-capex factor.

ideas.event: Goldman Sachs equities revenue rose 72% to $6.44 billion; EPS $17.01 vs $13.02 expected
chain: Goldman's equities blowout reflects an industry-wide surge in institutional trading and prime brokerage.
Morgan Stanley runs the largest equities franchise on the Street and reports Q3 shortly after Goldman.
Its consensus was set before Goldman's print showed how big the quarter was.
Read-through into Morgan Stanley's report.
ideas.name: Morgan Stanley
ideas.priced_in: The most obvious link on this list; bank stocks partly moved with Goldman on Oct 13. Short horizon on purpose. Update Oct 15: Morgan Stanley reported on Oct 14 with equity net revenues up 41% to $5.80 billion, versus 72% growth at Goldman, which meets the kill condition; the stock fell about 2.8% on the day.
ideas.kill: Morgan Stanley's equities revenue growth comes in well below Goldman's.

ideas.event: UnitedHealth said on Oct 13 that commercial medical cost trend is running north of the 11% it assumed for 2026, driven by acute-care intensity, specialty drugs and No Surprises Act arbitration, and that it expects the trend to persist into 2027.

source.title: Motley Fool: UnitedHealth Q3 2026 earnings call transcript

source2.title: Business Wire: Insperity Q3 2025 results and new UnitedHealthcare contract

chain: UnitedHealth sees commercial claims cost trend above 11% and is not assuming any slowdown into 2027.
UnitedHealthcare carries the health plan that Insperity offers to its clients' worksite employees, under a contract extended through 2028.
Insperity bears the gap between what it charges clients and the plan's claims cost: in Q3 2025 the same inpatient, outpatient and pharmacy trend cut its gross profit 15%.
Insperity (NSP), up about 36% this year and reporting Q3 on Oct 29 with an EPS guide of -$0.09 to $0.41, is exposed to a second year of above-plan trend.
ideas.name: Insperity
ideas.priced_in: Insurer read-throughs usually go to other insurers, not to employers that self-insure through a carrier. NSP rose into early October (about $49, up 36% YTD) with no sign of reacting to the UnitedHealth call. Risk: the lower $500,000 large-claim pooling level in the new contract shifts some cost back to UnitedHealthcare.
ideas.kill: Insperity's Oct 29 report shows benefits costs at or below plan and keeps the midpoint of its 2026 EPS guidance.
ideas.book: No AI-capex exposure; a short in staffing/HR services diversifies the book.

ideas.event: UnitedHealth said on Oct 13 that commercial medical cost trend is running north of 11%, citing acute healthcare service intensity among the drivers, and is pricing 2027 for the trend to persist.

source.title: Motley Fool: UnitedHealth Q3 2026 earnings call transcript

source2.title: inkl: HCA Healthcare's Q3 2026 earnings, what to expect

chain: An insurer's medical cost trend is a hospital's price and acuity mix seen from the other side.
UnitedHealth names acute-care service intensity in commercial plans as a driver of trend above 11%, the highest-margin payer class for hospitals.
The market has priced HCA for a worse payer mix after ACA subsidies lapsed: shares are about 18% below their 52-week high and Q3 EPS is expected to fall 3.3% to $6.73.
HCA, the largest US hospital operator, reports Oct 27, inside the horizon, with commercial intensity as a possible offset to the coverage losses.
ideas.name: HCA Healthcare
ideas.priced_in: HCA traded flat on Oct 13 while healthcare stocks lagged on J&J. The UnitedHealth call was read for UnitedHealth's own margins, not as a revenue signal for hospitals. Risk: lost exchange coverage outweighs higher commercial intensity.
ideas.kill: HCA's Oct 27 report shows same-facility revenue per equivalent admission growth below 3%, or another large insurer reports a clear slowdown in commercial cost trend before then.
ideas.book: No AI-capex exposure; diversifies the book.

ideas.event: Givaudan reported Q3 like-for-like sales growth of 8.6% versus a 4.7% consensus on Oct 13, with Fragrance & Beauty up 13.5% versus 6.6% expected; analysts estimate fine fragrance grew about 31%.

source.title: ESM Magazine (Reuters): Givaudan exceeds organic sales growth expectations in Q3

source2.title: Investing.com: Givaudan shares hit 15-month high as fragrance-led sales beat

chain: Givaudan makes the fragrance oils that perfume brands buy before they fill and ship bottles.
Its fine fragrance sales grew about 31% in Q3 and 15.3% over nine months, well above what analysts expected, even as luxury fashion weakens.
Supplier orders at that pace point to strong brand shipments over the next quarter or two.
Interparfums (IPAR), a fine-fragrance licensing pure play downgraded twice last month, reports on Nov 4.
ideas.name: Interparfums
ideas.priced_in: Givaudan rose 6.5-9% and European peers 1.6-3.1%, but IPAR gained only 1.5% on Oct 13 (to $114, versus a $129 52-week high). Part of Givaudan's growth is price increases passed on to customers, and its mix of brand customers is not disclosed.
ideas.kill: Interparfums cuts 2026 sales guidance on Nov 4, or Coty or Estee Lauder report falling fragrance sales before then.
ideas.book: Consumer, no AI-capex exposure; diversifies the book.

ideas.event: On Oct 15 the Fifth Circuit ruled that the FCC lacked authority to create USAC, the body that collects about $9 billion a year for the Universal Service Fund, and vacated the fourth-quarter 2025 contribution factor; the FCC said the order would not take effect for at least two months.

source.title: Investing.com (Reuters): US appeals court invalidates federal $9 billion telecom subsidy fund

source2.title: Broadband Breakfast: GCI Liberty CEO says Universal Service Fund is essential for Alaska

chain: The ruling attacks the body that collects and pays out the fund's money (schools and libraries, rural health care, rural broadband), not just one program.

GCI gets about 40% of its roughly $1 billion in annual revenue from the fund and is the largest E-Rate recipient in Alaska (nearly $700 million since July 2021), with $52 million of Rural Health Care receivables at year-end 2025.
Any pause or restructuring of collections puts both the revenue and the timing of those receivables at risk ahead of GCI's Nov 5 report.
GCI Liberty (GLIBK), probably the most fund-dependent listed US carrier, rose 2.6% on the day of the ruling, so the risk does not look priced.
ideas.name: GCI Liberty (Series C)
ideas.priced_in: GLIBK closed up 2.64% at $20.60 on Oct 15, and the Reuters story on the ruling ran that evening. The stock already sits near its 52-week low ($19.30, versus a $41.18 high), insiders bought about $13.6 million of shares over the past 90 days, and the Supreme Court upheld the fund's financing in June 2025. The FCC is likely to seek rehearing or a stay, so payments may never stop.
ideas.kill: The Fifth Circuit stays its order or grants rehearing en banc, Congress authorizes USAC, or the FCC confirms that disbursements will continue uninterrupted, before GCI's Nov 5 report.
ideas.book: Alaska telecom with no AI-capex link; diversifies the book. A short, so track it as a signal.

ideas.event: The Wall Street Journal reported on the evening of Oct 15 that US-Mexico talks to cut the 25% US tariff on Mexican cars and the 50% tariffs on steel and aluminum have stalled over Commerce Secretary Lutnick's objections; officials on both sides say talks continue.

source.title: Investing.com: U.S.-Mexico tariff deal stalls over Lutnick objections, WSJ reports

source2.title: StockAnalysis: Ternium Q2 2026 earnings call transcript

chain: The stalled deal would have cut Section 232 tariffs on Mexican cars, steel, aluminum and finished goods made from steel and aluminum.

On its Q2 call, Ternium said the tariffs make its Mexican industrial customers cautious, and that US-owned customers and auto makers (Mexico builds about 4 million vehicles a year) are waiting for a resolution before committing.
A stall pushes that demand back past Ternium's Nov 3 report and into 2027 contract talks.
Ternium (TX), a steelmaker focused on Mexico, trades near its 52-week high ($59.32) with its market value up 56% over the year, so a long delay is not priced.
ideas.name: Ternium
ideas.priced_in: TX fell 2.85% to $56.88 on Oct 15, before the report came out at about 8 PM ET. Mexico's deputy trade minister says talks are progressing, so the stall may be short. Ternium does not disclose how much of its volume goes to US-bound customers, and it is also gaining share from Asian imports in Mexico.
ideas.kill: The US and Mexico announce cuts to the Section 232 steel or auto tariffs, or Ternium guides higher Mexican shipments for Q4 on Nov 3.
ideas.book: Latin American steel with no AI-capex link; diversifies the book (CAT is the closest industrial overlap). A short, so track it as a signal.

ideas.event: Reuters reported on Oct 15 that the US is weighing letting buyers take sanctioned shadow-fleet tankers into mainstream trade; Kpler estimates only about 24 of the roughly 160 sanctioned supertankers could realistically rejoin.

source.title: Benzinga: Trump weighs shadow fleet sanctions relief; DHT, Frontline, International Seaways face rate risk

chain: About 160 VLCCs, roughly 22% of the commercial fleet, are under US sanctions; after age and Iranian ownership, Kpler counts only about 24 (about 3% of the fleet) that could rejoin mainstream trade.
CREA finds sanctioned tankers carried 57% of Russia's seaborne oil in September, so ships that switch would mostly leave a gap in the Russian trade rather than add net capacity.
DHT, a pure VLCC owner, had booked about 50% of its Q4 spot days at $509,100 per day, about three times the $167,100 its spot VLCCs earned in Q3.
DHT gave back its whole post-update gain on the relief talk, though the realistic capacity release is small; the Q4 bookings it already has are not in the price.
ideas.name: DHT Holdings
ideas.priced_in: DHT rose about 6.5% to $26.24 after its Oct 12 update, then fell to $23.60 by Oct 16 (about -10%) as the Gulf-China VLCC rate eased from Worldscale 841 to 776 on the relief talk and lower Gulf exports; premarket on Oct 19 it was $23.90. The VLCC ST3 was hit off Al Jubail on Oct 16, the IRGC claimed two supertankers hit mines on Oct 17 (unconfirmed), and about 217 ships were waiting at anchor off Fujairah and Khorfakkan on Oct 18, all after the close. Risk: attacks also cut Gulf export volumes, which Kpler says has already softened demand on the main VLCC route.
ideas.kill: Treasury clears substantially more than about 24 sanctioned VLCCs for mainstream trade, or DHT's Q3 report shows Q4 spot bookings well below the $509,100 per day disclosed on Oct 12.
ideas.book: Crude shipping with no AI-capex link; diversifies the book. Shares the Hormuz factor with the open STNG product-tanker idea.

ideas.event: China's statistics bureau reported on Oct 19 that September coal output fell 6.8% year on year to 385 million tons, as safety checks after a deadly May mine disaster kept Shanxi mines suspended heading into winter.

source.title: Oilprice.com: China's coal production slumps 6.8% as winter supply fears grow

source2.title: Peabody: Results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026

chain: Chinese output keeps falling into the heating season, with domestic thermal coal at three-year highs, coal prices up about 24% since mid-July, and Newcastle futures up 1.1% to $154.60/t.
Australian exporters repriced on Oct 19 (Whitehaven +4.8%, Yancoal +4.5%, New Hope +4.0%), after US markets had closed for the weekend.
Peabody's July guidance left about 4.1-4.7 million tons of 2026 seaborne thermal exports unpriced, roughly half of them priced off Newcastle, against a Q2 realized export price of $95.87/t.
Peabody (BTU), the US-listed owner of Australian thermal mines, has not traded since the data and reports Q3 around Oct 29; it closed Oct 16 at $23.89, in the lower part of its $20.06-41.14 range.
ideas.name: Peabody Energy
ideas.priced_in: BTU fell 0.5% on Oct 16. The stock has lagged coal prices because of commissioning problems at its Centurion met mine and weak Powder River Basin volumes, which remain the main risk to the idea. China's output has been declining since April, so part of the price strength is already known; the new facts are the September figure and the Australian repricing that US-listed coal has not yet matched.
ideas.kill: Newcastle coal futures fall back below about $140/t, or Peabody's Q3 report cuts seaborne thermal volume guidance or Centurion targets again.
ideas.book: Coal with no AI-capex link; diversifies the book (minor overlap with CAT through mining demand).
